caption: Our timber pergola in the sensory garden, all locally sourced wood with a sunny yellow plinth and gravel paths underfoot. Hawthorn and willow plantings give shade and scent for the children on the school side (May 2026)
The drystone amphitheatre in the sensory garden, with hazel and willow filling out behind. A great little outdoor classroom for the school (May 2026)
A carved wooden sculpture in the sensory garden, made from a recycled tree stump and tucked in among the willows. A real talking point for the kids (May 2026)

Volunteer building a living willow dome in the sensory garden. Once these rods root and leaf out they'll create a brilliant natural play and shelter feature, and the early catkins are great for bees too (March 2026)

Work underway on the sensory garden timber gateway and entrance, weaving living willow rods into the boundary planting alongside natural stone and reclaimed timber. All sustainable materials creating a lovely outdoor classroom space right beside the school (March 2026)
